sections.title: Greeting
sections.line: Paul writes as an apostle by God's will, not his own.

sections.title: Blessed before the foundation
sections.line: Election stated as praise rather than posed as a problem.

sections.title: Redemption and the disclosed mystery
sections.line: The blood-bought forgiveness reveals a plan to unite everything.

sections.title: Sealed and guaranteed
sections.line: The Spirit is the down payment on an inheritance not yet paid out.

sections.title: Prayer to see what is already true
sections.line: Paul asks not for more gifts but for eyes to see them.

themes.note: Every blessing is located in him, never merely alongside him.
Each gift is traced back to God's purpose, not to our merit.

themes.theme: To the praise of his glory
themes.note: The refrain that closes each movement, naming the point.
Resurrection power is the measure of what works in believers.

references.why: Humanity's mandate over creation is claimed for Christ, so the church's head already rules everything.
Echoes Nebuchadnezzar's boast of mighty power, relocating that language from a proud king to God.

purpose: Paul wants us to know our standing was settled before the world began, so that nothing that happens later can unsettle it.
He wants us to believe God has one plan — to bring everything together in Christ — so that our small salvation is read as part of it.
He prays we would see the power already at work in us, because it is the same power that raised Christ from the dead.
